rv.q: Fortunately, “The Visit” does speak clearly in Tresnjak’s production, beautifully arrayed on scenic designer Alexander Dodge’s inventive simulacrum of the town.
And with lead performances like Mays' and Hamilton's, the production is — sorry to do this here — worth your visit.
The imbalance of dark humor and disturbing pathos is deftly handled by the cast, which is uniformly superb.
The Visit is an absorbing and timely indictment of that oxymoron called humanity.
With the ambitiousness of its programming, and the quality of its productions, Pasadena Playhouse is on a streak.
Pasadena Playhouse once again delivers a Broadway-caliber revival that doesn't stint an iota where production values or cast size is concerned.

cn.t: Critics praise this visually stunning revival of Dürrenmatt's dark morality play, with director Darko Tresnjak and star Jefferson Mays delivering another triumph after their acclaimed "Amadeus," offering timely commentary on greed and humanity's capacity for cruelty.
